# Buck (chopper) with an RL load: the PWM is generated here in controle.py and the average current loop is a PI with
# reference feedforward, updated once per switching period.
#
# Every Ts (in the panel: 2 µs, with Δt = 1 µs), the code:
#   1. generates the sawtooth carrier (0 → 1, at fsw) from the time t;
#   2. sums i_L to take the average over the switching period (the ripple here is ~3 A on 10 A: a single point would be off);
#   3. at the start of each period, updates the duty cycle d = d_ff + (Kp·error + Ki·integral)/Vdc,
#      with the error on the average of the previous period;
#   4. compares the carrier with d and returns the switch command: g = 1 (S.1 on) or 0 (off).
# The actuation "g" is CONST.1, which goes into GATE.1, coupled to the switch S.1 (on with input > 0.5).
#
# Tuning (plant i_L/d = Vdc/(R + sL); the controller's 1/Vdc cancels the converter gain → plant 1/(R + sL)):
#   - Ki/Kp = R/L = 2000 rad/s: the PI zero cancels the load pole, and the open loop becomes Kp/(sL);
#   - crossover at fc = fsw/10 = 500 Hz (previously 300 Hz) → Kp = 2π·fc·L = 3.1416 and Ki = Kp·R/L = 6283.
#     The loop delay (average centered on the previous period + duty only in the next period) is ~Tsw = 200 µs,
#     which at 500 Hz takes 36° of phase and leaves ~54° of margin. Above fsw/10 the period average no longer
#     represents the dynamics and the tuning stops making sense;
#   - feedforward d_ff = k_ff·R·i_ref/Vdc: the steady-state duty, taken straight from the model. With it the reference
#     step (and the start-up) already show up in the duty in the same period, without waiting for the integral to wind up
#     to the operating point. k_ff = 0 goes back to the PI-only behavior, for comparison;
#   - anti-windup by back-calculation: when d saturates, the integral is recomputed from the duty actually applied,
#     instead of just freezing — so the output leaves saturation with no delay.
#
# What the tuning does not change: d only exists in steps of Ts·fsw (2 µs × 5 kHz = 1 %), so the PI alternates between two
# neighboring steps (t_on of 40/42 µs at d ≈ 0.2), and the 3.2 A peak-to-peak ripple comes from L·fsw, not from the control.

def iniciar(p, e):
    e["periodo"] = -1      # index of the current switching period
    e["soma"] = 0.0        # sum of i_L over the period (for the average)
    e["n"] = 0
    e["integral"] = 0.0
    e["i_med"] = 0.0       # average of i_L over the last period
    e["erro"] = 0.0
    # start already at the steady-state duty: the start-up does not wait for the integral to rise
    e["d"] = min(p["dmax"], max(0.0, p["k_ff"] * p["R"] * p["i_ref"] / p["Vdc"]))


def passo(t, m, p, e):
    fsw = p["fsw"]
    k = int(t * fsw + 1e-9)                 # current switching period (the 1e-9 avoids a rounding error at the edge)
    portadora = t * fsw - k                 # sawtooth, 0 → 1

    if k != e["periodo"]:                   # a new period started: update the duty with the average of the previous one
        if e["n"] > 0:
            i_med = e["soma"] / e["n"]
            erro = p["i_ref"] - i_med
            d_ff = p["k_ff"] * p["R"] * p["i_ref"] / p["Vdc"]   # steady-state duty (load model)
            integral = e["integral"] + erro / fsw               # integration step = Tsw (updates 1×/period)
            d = d_ff + (p["Kp"] * erro + p["Ki"] * integral) / p["Vdc"]
            d_sat = min(p["dmax"], max(0.0, d))
            if d != d_sat and p["Ki"] != 0.0:                   # anti-windup: recompute the integral from the saturated duty
                integral = (p["Vdc"] * (d_sat - d_ff) - p["Kp"] * erro) / p["Ki"]
            e["integral"] = integral
            e["d"] = d_sat
            e["i_med"] = i_med
            e["erro"] = erro
        e["periodo"], e["soma"], e["n"] = k, 0.0, 0

    e["soma"] += m["i_L"]
    e["n"] += 1

    g = 1.0 if portadora < e["d"] else 0.0  # PWM: the switch stays on while the carrier is below d
    scope("portadora", portadora)            # scope(): the same names in every sample (the columns are fixed on the 1st)
    scope("d", e["d"])
    scope("i_med", e["i_med"])
    scope("i_ref", p["i_ref"])
    scope("erro", e["erro"])
    return {"g": g}
